answers.answer: 1. Start with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it. 2. Draw 8 Zoo cards, keep 4 and discard 4; draw 2 Final Scoring cards and keep them hidden. 3. Put Animals side I in slot 1; put the other four action cards randomly in slots 2–5, all side I. 4. Appeal starts at 0/1/2/3 for first/second/third/fourth player, respectively.

1. Put 3 base projects face up below the Association board in 2- and 3-player games; put 4 there with 4 players. 2. In a 2-player game, block the left level of the left project, middle level of the middle project, right level of the right project, and all three spaces in the donation area's left column. 3. With 3 or 4 players, no project levels or donation spaces are blocked at setup. 4. Reveal the six-card display after all players select starting hands.

1. Using slot 4, remove that used card, shift cards from slots 1–3 one slot right, and put the used card in slot 1. 2. Set strength before the action; each X-token spent adds 1 strength, and cannot exceed five held. 3. Bonuses gained earlier in an action can fund later steps; X-tokens gained during it cannot boost it. 4. Resolve after-finishing effects after completing the action and moving cards.
answers.evidence: Taking a turn; X-tokens; After finishing.

answers.answer: 1. You cannot take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings; use the alternative X-token action if unable or unwilling to perform a regular action. 2. Select an Action card, move it to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right, then take exactly 1 X-token. 3. The card's strength and upgrade state do not matter; unavailable if already holding 5 X-tokens.

1. Reaching the last Break-track space grants the triggering player 1 X-token; ignore extra movement beyond that space. 2. Finish the current turn, then conduct the break for everyone. 3. After the break, reset the Break token to its player-count starting space; play continues clockwise with the next player.

1. Both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. Side I chooses deck draw per its table (maximum 3, with any required discard from a new or held card) or exactly one display card at strength 5+, regardless of reputation. 2. Side II draws from deck and/or from display within reputation range in any order; at strength 5 it draws 4 and discards 1. Snap is exactly one display card at strength 3+ and ignores reputation on either side; no deck draw. 3. Refill display after turn completion; no in-turn hand limit, discard down only at breaks (normally 3, or 5 with hand-limit university).
answers.evidence: Cards action; Reputation track and display; Hand size.

answers.answer: 1. Reputation range includes the display folder matching your reputation and all lower-numbered folders. 2. Reputation 10+ requires upgraded Cards; at 15, each additional reputation step gives 1 appeal. 3. You may not inspect the discard pile during play.
answers.evidence: Reputation spaces and rewards; Reputation track and display.

answers.answer: 1. Build I builds exactly one building of size at most strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size at most strength, never two identical in that action. Buildings cost 2 money per space. 2. First building must cover a border space; later buildings touch an existing building by an edge. Cannot build beyond map, overlap or cover water/rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. 3. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. Each pavilion immediately gives 1 appeal once.

1. Build I allows standard enclosures, kiosks, pavilions and one Petting Zoo; Build II additionally allows one Reptile House and one Large Bird Aviary. A zoo may have at most one of each special enclosure. 2. Unique buildings cannot be built with Build; they enter through Sponsor cards. 3. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately gives 7 appeal, including coverage by other effects.
answers.evidence: Buildings available through Build; Build action.

answers.answer: 1. Yes: benefits gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and activated workers, can be used in later steps. Pay an item's cost before receiving that item's benefit. 2. Immediate effects resolve during the action; after-finishing effects wait until the action and card movement are complete. 3. For simultaneous effects, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: X-tokens; Animals action; Multiple simultaneous effects.

answers.answer: 1. Check all card conditions, pay full cost (matching partner zoo discounts 3 money per matching continent icon), then house the animal legally; play from hand on side I, and side II can also play in-range display animals with folder cost. 2. Standard housing needs an empty enclosure at least the printed size, then flip it occupied; Petting Zoo animals use Petting Zoo, and eligible reptiles/birds can use special-enclosure capacity marked with tokens. 3. Meet water/rock adjacency for chosen housing, counting distinct adjacent hexes. Effects follow admission; after-finishing effects wait until end of Animals action and simultaneous effects may be ordered by you.

1. Animals II may play in-range display animals, paying extra money equal to their folder number; mix hand/display as desired and refill only after turn end. 2. At strength 5+, you may gain 1 reputation first, before playing animals, extending range. 3. It also permits upgrade-required animal conditions.

1. Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary may you move eligible matching animals, each chosen separately, if terrain requirements and capacity fit. 2. For each moved animal, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements; if none, smallest meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. 3. Mark occupancy in the new special enclosure with supply tokens for the animal's indicated capacity; relocation is distinct from release.
answers.evidence: Moving existing animals into a newly built special enclosure.

answers.answer: 1. Association tasks require strength 2 for +2 reputation, 3 for partner zoo, 4 for university, and 5 for conservation project work. 2. Side I performs exactly one task; Side II performs one or more different tasks whose total value does not exceed action strength. 3. Each task requires 1 worker, or 2 if one of yours is already there; with 3 of yours there, cannot repeat before break. Other players' workers do not matter.

1. Take partner zoos and universities from available Association-board tiles and place on lowest empty matching map spaces, resolving printed space bonuses immediately; university also grants its printed reputation. 2. No duplicate continents among partner zoos, maximum 4; third/fourth requires Association II. Universities cannot be duplicated. 3. Hand-limit university raises hand limit from 3 to 5; other universities do not affect it. Board tiles restock at breaks except types owned by everyone.
answers.evidence: Setup; University tiles; Association action; Break procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Conservation project cards can be played from hand, or from in-range display with Association II (pay folder cost); new card enters above Association board. Base projects stay below. 2. Support a project only once normally, and only an unoccupied reward level (no player's token); meet a condition, place one token from left map edge, then take reward and uncover map bonus in either order. 3. If project overflow discards a card, return tokens to owners' supplies; their map bonuses remain active.

1. A release project matches the animal's printed standard-enclosure requirement: 2− = size 1–2; 3 = size 3; 4+ = size 4–5, regardless of actual housing. 2. Lose only its printed appeal before conservation; discard animal and lose its icons, but retain conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier earned effects. New release project play gives 1 reputation; later support does not. 3. Remove special-enclosure tokens if possible, otherwise flip smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements, else size alone, else none.

1. Sponsors I plays exactly one hand card if strength meets its level and conditions; or advance Break token by strength and take that much money. 2. Sponsors II may play one or more cards from hand/display in reputation range; display costs folder number, and total levels must be at most strength +1. Resolve each card fully before next, deferring after-finishing effects. 3. Its money option advances the Break token and pays twice the strength; do not reduce money for fewer remaining spaces.
answers.evidence: Sponsors action says full money even if token does not need all steps, but double-money option states twice; exact edge-case interaction of remaining break steps is not separately spelled out.

answers.answer: 1. Break order: discard to hand limit (3, or 5 with hand-limit university); clear action-card tokens; recall workers/restock tiles; discard display folders 1–2 and refill; take incomes; reset break track. 2. Kiosk earns 1 per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not qualify, empty special enclosures do. 3. For multiple display-taking players during income, resolve clockwise from break initiator and refill after each affected player's income before the next chooses.

1. At 2 conservation choose upgrade or activate worker; at 5 and 8 choose 5 money or available bonus tile; first player reaching 10 makes everyone discard one Final Scoring card. 2. Check end at end of own turn or during break when Appeal and Conservation are in same scoring area or pass; a zoo receiving appeal on another's turn checks at its own turn end or break. Triggering player completes turn; others take one more (break trigger: all players one more). 3. Each Final Scoring card scores at most 4 conservation. VP = appeal minus lowest appeal in your conservation scoring area; highest positive wins, tiebreak most project supports then shared victory.

1. Shuffle 9 Bonus tiles and place random tiles on the four blank yellow spaces beside conservation track (two at 5 and two at 8); leave icon spaces empty and return other five to box. 2. Components are not limiting: if stock runs out, use a suitable substitute; explicit per-zoo limits and board availability still apply.

1. Advanced Maps 1–8: take two random maps and choose one, or lay out player count +1 and choose in reverse play order; return unselected maps. 2. Map A starts with empty 3-space enclosure and a kiosk on indicated spaces; printed kiosk counts as built.
1. Seven project-support tokens start on designated spaces at the left edge of zoo map. 2. Hire workers from lowest reserve space upward. 3. Some maps grant conservation when hiring the last worker.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C2–C3; Association worker supply.

answers.answer: 1. Flip a chosen side-I card to side II in its current slot; improved action is available from your next action, but counts as upgraded for conditions immediately. 2. Current action retains its starting strength/type. 3. There are only four upgrade opportunities and one permits an alternative, so all five cards cannot be upgraded.
1. Strength 1: draw 1/discard 1; 2: 1/0; 3: 2/1; 4: 2/0; 5+: 3/1. 2. Required discard may be a newly drawn card or a card already in hand.

1. The seven categories are bird, herbivore, predator, primate, reptile, bear and Petting Zoo animal. 2. Include bear and Petting Zoo animal unless explicitly excluded; bears may also have herbivore/predator icons.

1. Donation requires at least one Association task in same action, no worker, maximum one per Association action; pay smallest visible cost and gain 1 conservation. 2. Costs are 2, 5, 5, 7, 7, 10, 10, then repeatable 12; cover paid spaces with a supply token, skip spaces blocked at setup. 3. Once all but last are covered, each donation costs 12 and places no further token.

1. Zoo icons include Animal/Sponsor upper-right icons, Animal and unique-building Sponsor water/rock requirements, and partner-zoo/university continent/research icons. Exclude play conditions, conservation-project icons, university reputation and hand-limit mark. 2. Own card icons count; doubles count twice, but repeated icon types count once for different-type effects. 3. Card text overrides general rules.
answers.evidence: Counting icons in your zoo; shared principles.

answers.answer: 1. Terrain adjacency counts distinct water/rock hexes, not edges; multiple edges to one hex count once. 2. Connected regions do not turn one adjacent hex into multiple; decorative illustrations on tiles do not count as terrain spaces.

1. Playing a new Release into the Wild project grants the player who plays it 1 reputation; later support grants none. 2. Breeding Program projects use the same condition at all three levels, so choose any available reward space when condition is met.
answers.evidence: Release projects; Breeding Program project cards.

answers.answer: 1. In X:Y, X is condition and Y reward. 2. Condition without number or marked “per” pays once per fulfillment; numbered threshold pays once, and with several thresholds use highest met.

1. Connected means an uncovered space sharing an edge with a covered space; isolated has no adjacent covered space. 2. Border space lacks a neighboring map hex on at least one of six sides. 3. Your zoo includes your played cards, map and personal supply; any zoo includes all players' equivalents.

1. Unique building Sponsor requires placing matching tile when played; if impossible, cannot play card. 2. Place colored face up, freely rotate, do not flip; ordinary placement and terrain rules apply, no size-based payment. They are not enclosures, house no animals and are not terrain. 3. Sponsor cannot be played if the tile cannot legally fit.

1. Both named Action and Determination resolve after finishing Animals and moving Animals card to slot 1; use granted Action card normally and move it to slot 1 after. 2. Named action cannot be replaced by X-token action; Determination (Any Action) can choose X-token action.

1. Assertion/Dominance search unused face-down base-project deck for chosen/named card, take into hand and return deck. 2. Dominance does nothing if named project already in play. 3. Later play and immediately support it above Association board, not in base row below.

1. Boost/Clever resolve after Animals and its card movement. 2. Clever moves chosen card to slot 1, shifting cards formerly to its left right. Boost puts named card in slot 1 or 5; moving to 5 shifts cards formerly to its right left.

1. All affected zoos need at least 5 appeal; the animal's appeal may be awarded before or after ability, so generally does not count for target eligibility. 2. In multiplayer, group may use the cards' solo alternative text instead without playing solo mode.

1. Each affected other zoo places Constriction on its own slot-5 card if ahead on one track; if ahead on both, on its own slot-4 and slot-5 cards. Never stack; return duplicate. 2. Reduces strength by 2 for each multiplied execution; X-tokens restore it. Remove after acting or without effect at break.
1. At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least 1, take the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least slot 3.

1. Digging 2 allows up to two choices, choosing anew after each: discard a display card and immediately replenish, or discard hand card then draw one deck card. 2. Display replenishment shifts higher folders down and draws into folder 6.

1. Flock animal can avoid new enclosure if another zoo herbivore requires at least its standard size. Same qualifying herbivore can host any number; it need not be flock animal. 2. Without host, house normally; later non-flock herbivore cannot share its enclosure. 3. Releasing flock animal follows normal release/fallback enclosure freeing; no need to track original residents.
1. Full-throated activates lowest reserve worker onto notepad for immediate use. 2. Take map's conservation reward if hiring last worker. 3. With all workers active, ability has no effect.
1. Hunter reveals specified number of deck cards; if none is Animal, discard all revealed cards.

1. Hypnosis targets highest-appeal zoo with at least 5 appeal; choose among tied leaders; self-target has no effect. 2. Copy only slot 1–3 using target card's side; spend your own X-tokens, move borrowed card to slot 1 normally. 3. Venom/Constriction on it apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used.

1. Multiplier is placed on named Action card, or any card (including Animals) if from bonus tile. Its next use executes twice at same base strength; move card after both. Each X-token boosts one execution; each extra Multiplier adds one execution. 2. Defer after-finishing effects until all done; break waits until entire turn ends. Return used tokens to supply; clear unused at break.

1. Two Multiplier tokens permit up to three sequential actions, not four. 2. Each execution can choose different regular options; multiplied alternative X-token action can take two X-tokens subject to cap, but cannot mix one X-token action and one regular action.

1. Peacocking permits placing Large Bird Aviary before Build II if zoo lacks one and legal site exists. Upgrade-marked spaces still require Build II. 2. Posturing follows normal placement rules including kiosk spacing; place multiple buildings sequentially.
1. Petting Zoo animals grant appeal 3/6/9 for first/second/third; one Petting Zoo holds maximum three. 2. They count as small animals.

1. Acting player chooses among tied leaders separately for Pilfering 1 and each Pilfering 2 target. Conservation target needs at least 1 conservation; if all zero, that part has no effect. 2. Self-target has no effect; Pilfering 2 still resolves its separate highest-appeal target.

1. Target chooses five money or random hand-card draw; never Final Scoring cards. 2. With no hand cards target gives five money; with under five money gives a card; with neither gives all current money, including zero. 3. Repeated pilferings resolve sequentially; target may choose differently each time.

1. Pouch tucks up to X hand cards under animal for 2 appeal each; they have no function and are discarded if animal released, while appeal remains. 2. Sunbathing sells up to X hand cards for 4 money each; sold cards go to discard pile.

1. Extra Final Scoring card from Resistance drawn before 10 conservation joins choice when discarding one at milestone. 2. At game end score every remaining Final Scoring card; each has its own 4-conservation cap.
1. Shuffle discard pile face down, draw randomly, then make stated selection and return discard pile face up. Scavenging 3 draws 3, keeps 1, discards others.

1. Snapping takes exactly one display card regardless of reputation; no deck alternative. 2. Sponsor Magnet takes display Sponsors regardless of range; if none, nothing happens. Ordinary end-of-turn refill applies.

1. Venom places X tokens on affected player's lowest-slot cards first, one per card; duplicates return. Using a marked card removes its token and avoids all fees that turn. 2. Pay 2 money at turn end only if no token removed and at least one remains; if unable, undo turn and choose another action. Break clears unused tokens.
1. Veterinarian gives 2/5/10 money for 1/2/3 universities; conservation project support requires strength 4 instead of 5; final scoring gives 1 conservation with three universities.
1. Medical Breakthrough counts previously supported projects by tokens missing from left map edge and gives 2 appeal each. At each break it gives 1 conservation.

1. Basic Research counts distinct continent and animal-category icon types together, excludes research, duplicates and double icons as repeats. Gain 1 conservation per pair, rounding down; every other player gets 2 money per conservation gained.
1. Science Library gives 1 appeal per research icon on play. Whenever any player plays a research icon, its owner gains 2 money. Final: 1 conservation with five different animal categories.
1. Expert on Americas gives 1 appeal per Americas icon on play; each Americas icon played allows a free kiosk with ordinary placement/spacing rules. Final: 1 conservation with at least five kiosks.
1. Expert on Australia gives 1 appeal per Australia icon on play; for each Australia icon played, may tuck a hand card under it for 2 appeal. Tucked cards have no further function.

1. Each card stores two of your supply tokens on itself; for supporting a base project below board, return exactly one as any icon, not both for same project. Above-board base-origin cards do not qualify. 2. Final: 1 conservation with five or more project supports, counted by missing map-edge tokens.

1. Engineer lets each Build action add one extra copy of a building built in that action, without extra strength, paying normal cost and placement; only one extra total, and special enclosures retain one-per-type limit. 2. Final gives 5 appeal with full map except water/rock.

1. Gives 2 money per water/rock icon. You may cover terrain spaces and ignore terrain requirements of animals/unique buildings, though printed terrain icons still count. 2. Covered terrain stops counting for Hydrologist, Geologist and Architectural Zoo; full map need not cover terrain. 3. Final gives 2 appeal per water-rock icon pair, max 3.

1. Each actual placement bonus on border space gives extra choice of any uncovered placement bonus, not necessarily border; multiple triggers grant multiple choices, same or different. Resolve chosen order. 2. Final: 1 conservation when all building border spaces covered, excluding water/rock.

1. Migration Recording gives 1 X-token. Each release-project support gives 1 extra conservation; may support same release project repeatedly with different qualifying animals, max one token on that project per Association action. 2. Each token is a separate support for other effects.

1. Gives 1 X-token and immunity to Venom, Constriction, Hypnosis and Pilfering. For Hypnosis/Pilfering ignore your counters and find next qualifying player. Final: 1 conservation with all five continents.

1. Permanently choose small or large, mark with supply token, reveal deck until finding one of chosen type, keep it and discard others. 2. Chosen smalls gain 2 extra appeal; chosen large gain 4. Cannot play opposite size class; size-3 remain legal without bonus.

1. WAZA Small Animals Program gives 2 money per small animal on play. An Animals action containing only small animals may play one additional small animal from hand at normal cost/rules, then take one small display animal into hand regardless of reputation; may take it even if declining extra play. Mixed small/large prevents effect.

1. Hydrologist gives 1 appeal per water icon on play. Each newly covered space adjacent to water pays 1 money, even multiple spaces in one building; each space pays only once despite multiple adjacent water hexes. Final: 1 conservation if no water hex is isolated.
1. Barred Owl Hut is a unique building; place its tile. Each bird icon played triggers drawing two deck cards, keeping one and discarding the other.
1. Place Sea Turtle Tank adjacent to water. Each reptile icon played lets you sell up to two hand cards for 4 money each; discard sold cards.

1. Spotted Hyena Compound must be adjacent to rock. Each predator icon played triggers Hunter with draws equal to your total predator icons. A new double-predator triggers two sequential Hunters, counting both new icons for the second.

1. Okapi Stable enters with three supply tokens. Per herbivore icon played, spend one token and pay money equal to a hand Sponsor's level to play that Sponsor under normal conditions. Its own icon may trigger on play; three uses total.

1. Zoo School gives 1 reputation and 1 conservation, place unique building covering at least two border spaces, then take one in-range display card or draw one deck card; order simultaneous benefits as you choose.

1. Side Entrance is a unique building placed across two border spaces and need not touch existing building; later buildings may attach. 2. Break income is 2 money per adjacent building except empty standard enclosures. Adjacent kiosks count it for their income. 3. Final: 5 appeal with full map excluding water/rock.

1. Native Farm Animals gives 1 appeal per connected uncovered building border space, not terrain. 2. Final gives 1 conservation per six contiguous empty building spaces, evaluating each group separately; e.g. groups 13,6,3,2 yield 3 total. Upgrade-marked spaces count even without Build II; terrain spaces do not.

1. Explorer gives 2 money per different continent/category icon on play, excluding research. 2. Each category or continent newly introduced later gives 1 appeal and 2 money; a double identical new icon gets novelty reward once.

1. WAZA Large Animal Program may build free size-5 standard enclosure under normal placement rules. For each large animal, ignore one left-side card condition, but not terrain; Research Institute stacks to ignore two conditions.
1. Biodiverse Zoo gives 1 conservation for each category where your zoo has more icons than player to your right, max 4. If they have none in category, one of yours suffices.

1. Map 1 Observation Tower affects standard enclosures adjacent to tower hex itself; special enclosures do not qualify. Housing there gains its two appeal again after an animal was released. Tower is not a building for kiosk income.

1. Map 2 Outdoor Areas: standard enclosure touching the Outdoor Area hex counts two spaces larger for all purposes after placement, including release/relocation; cannot ignore. No special enclosure effect; Area is not a building.

1. Map 4 Commercial Harbor activates when a building is on adjacent building space; first building may start beside Harbor but need not. 2. Discard ability usable once per own turn before/during/after action, never break or another turn. Harbor is not a building.

1. Park Restaurant income is one per adjacent covered hex, including empty enclosures and each hex of multi-space building. It is not a building and yields no kiosk income. 2. Its special-enclosure bonus grants one free Reptile House OR Large Bird Aviary, even before Build II; normal other placement rules apply.

1. Hollywood Hills H spaces covered by buildings under ordinary placement; reveal deck until Sponsor, keep it and discard others. H is not placement bonus and does not trigger Archaeologist. 2. Once all 3 covered, Sponsor levels are each one lower. Partner third/fourth still require Association II; upgrade-marked spaces still require Build II.
1. Paid-Sponsor bonus costs money equal to Sponsor's level, requires its normal conditions, and card comes from hand even with Sponsors II. 2. Sponsors Action card stays in its current slot.
1. Appeal cannot exceed 113 and conservation cannot exceed 41; gains beyond those track ends are lost.

1. Venom targets every other higher-appeal zoo meeting 5 appeal; Hypnosis highest appeal at least 5 (ties chosen by actor), copies slot 1–3; Pilfering 1 highest appeal, Pilfering 2 highest appeal and most conservation separately, each target at least 5 appeal and conservation target at least 1 conservation, ties chosen by actor. 2. Constriction targets every other zoo with at least 5 appeal ahead on appeal and/or conservation: one token on its slot 5 if ahead one track; tokens on slots 4 and 5 if ahead both.

1. Partner-zoo animal condition requires a partner from that animal's continent; Sponsor partner condition accepts any continent. 2. Maximum-25 condition means may play only at appeal 25 or less, not a general cap; minimum-reputation requires at least printed value. 3. −1 condition bonus ignores one left-edge requirement only; other conditions and terrain remain.
1. Digging 2 offers up to two selections, each either discard display card and immediately replenish it, or discard hand card then draw one deck card; choices may differ.

1. When replenishing after display cards taken, move higher-folder cards down in their existing order, then fill empty folders from deck. Digging discard refills immediately by shifting down and drawing into folder 6. Break refill discards folders 1–2, compacts and refills. Exact broader “final empty folders” wording is not separately stated beyond filling empty spaces from deck.
answers.evidence: Reputation track and display; Digging 2; Break procedure.

answers.answer: 1. Build standard enclosure empty-side up, showing yellow border/size. Each placement bonus space covered is awarded immediately once; turning it occupied later does not award again.
1. At first 10-conservation milestone, each player discards one Final Scoring card face down under remaining pile.

1. Randomly determine start player; play clockwise, one turn at a time, without formal rounds. 2. On a turn take one regular Action card action; complete and move it before after-finishing effects. Additional granted actions/bonuses may follow, but the normal turn begins with one action.
1. If nobody reaches 10 conservation before game end, all players discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
